# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS. Cached routes disappear behind an indefinite spinner; no initial acknowledgment appears for five seconds; a fake 90% bar never advances; failure leaves no retry; retry creates overlapping requests and duplicates results.

# Apple HIG: status

Choose by meaning: progress indicates an operation completing, a gauge locates a value in a range, a rating expresses rank, and Activity rings exclusively represent personal Move/Exercise/Stand data. Check honesty, accessible labels, cancellation, and the exact platform component before styling.

Read the relevant article below before prescribing behavior. Its platform sections qualify shared guidance; absence of a platform-specific section does not imply unsupported behavior. Articles are original guidance tied to the dated official source.

- [Activity rings](references/activity-rings.md)
- [Gauges](references/gauges.md)
- [Progress indicators](references/progress-indicators.md)
- [Rating indicators](references/rating-indicators.md)

# Loading Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/loading) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Load content without interrupting useful interaction, ideally before waiting becomes noticeable. ## Best practices Show useful scaffolding, graphics, or placeholders promptly and replace them as real content arrives. Continue loading in the background while people use other features. For unavoidable waits, offer relevant tips or engaging content matched to the likely duration without repetitive loops. Schedule large assets with background-download mechanisms after install, during updates, or other nondisruptive periods to improve installation and startup. ## Showing progress If loading lasts more than a moment or two, show that work continues and give an estimate where possible. Use determinate progress for measurable work and indeterminate for unknown duration. Games can use a thematic custom loading view where standard progress styling would feel out of place. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Prefer immediate content and avoid wait indicators when possible. For a brief unavoidable second or two, an indicator is preferable to a blank display. Application advice: longer waits should not encourage prolonged wrist watching. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Launching](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/launching) [Progress indicators](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators) #### Developer documentation #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024.

# Progress indicators Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Progress UI is temporary feedback during work, disappearing when it finishes. Determinate indicators represent measurable completion with a leading-to-trailing bar or clockwise circular fill. Indeterminate indicators communicate ongoing activity without a completion estimate; every platform has a spinner, and macOS also has an indeterminate bar. ## Best practices Prefer measurable progress when possible and report it honestly. Estimate the whole operation so an early sprint to 90% does not conceal a much longer final stage. Keep activity visibly ongoing, and explain stalls with a useful recovery route. When duration becomes known, an indeterminate bar can become determinate; avoid changing a spinner into a differently shaped bar midtask because that disrupts layout and interpretation. Add a short, specific task description only when it supplies real context. Choose a consistent place for status. Allow cancellation where it is safe; offer pause as well when cancel would discard useful partial work. Explain consequential cancellation and let the person either confirm it or resume. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or visionOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS #### Refresh content controls Pull-to-refresh reveals an activity indicator when people drag down a content view. It supplements periodic automatic refreshes rather than making users responsible for every update. An optional title should convey useful content context, such as the previous update time, rather than explaining the pull gesture or merely restating that loading is occurring. ### macOS Both animated bars and spinners can represent indeterminate work. Prefer a small spinner for asynchronous background operations or tight spaces, such as beside a control or within a field. Usually omit spinner labels when the initiating action already explains the activity. ### watchOS Progress bars, circular fills, and spinners default to white against the scene background. Tint can customize their color. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — UIKit — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 12, 2023, June 5, 2023.

# Feedback Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Feedback communicates state, outcomes, consequences, and recovery. Match delivery intensity to significance: passive status can remain available in context; unexpected irreversible loss needs attention before it happens. ## Best practices Make feedback accessible through complementary visual, text, sound, and haptic signals rather than relying on one sense. Put routine state near the relevant item. Reserve alerts for critical, ideally actionable information. Warn before unexpected irreversible data loss, while avoiding warnings for ordinary expected deletion. Confirm completion when the task is significant, such as a payment, rather than adding noise to every successful action. When a command cannot run, explain the reason and how to proceed. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Avoid indeterminate wait indicators that imply people must keep watching. Reassure them when a notification will communicate completion instead. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio) [Playing haptics](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-haptics) [Motion](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion) #### Developer documentation — UIKit #### Videos

item.text: The supplied description identifies five problems: hidden cached routes, delayed acknowledgment, fabricated progress, no recovery after failure, and duplicate-producing retries. The local HIG guidance supports preserving useful content and providing honest feedback and recovery. I’ll specify request coordination as an engineering decision, since HIG doesn’t prescribe that mechanism.

# iPhone route planner: loading and retry audit

## Scope and decisions

Audit input: `interface.md`, a textual description of an iOS interface. Findings below are verified against that description, not observed in a running app. Priority reflects task impact, not measured frequency. All five should be corrected before accepting this flow.

Keep cached routes visible while refreshing, acknowledge actions promptly, use honest indeterminate activity when completion is unknown, and provide contextual recovery. Coordinate requests so retries cannot duplicate results or overwrite a newer route search. Use framework-agnostic state and rendering; no Apple SDK is required by this specification.

The installed apple-hig root was read explicitly, followed by the Patterns and Status family procedures, the topic-index entries for loading/progress/feedback, and their local source guides. Source links below identify the official articles recorded in those local guides; no web content was fetched.

## Ranked verified findings

| Rank | Supplied evidence | Effect and decision | Guidance and qualification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — High | “retry creates overlapping requests and duplicates results” | Retrying corrupts the route list and can allow stale responses to win. Permit one active request for the current query, ignore obsolete responses, and replace results atomically with unique route identities. | [Feedback — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback#Best-practices) supports understandable state and outcomes. Request tokens, deduplication, and atomic replacement are engineering decisions, not prescribed HIG mechanisms. |
| 2 — High | “failure leaves no retry” | A failed search becomes a dead end. End activity, explain the failure in context, retain query and cached content, and offer Retry. | [Progress indicators — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators#Best-practices) calls for explaining stalls with recovery; [Feedback — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback#Best-practices) calls for explaining why a command cannot run and how to proceed. |
| 3 — High | “Cached routes disappear behind an indefinite spinner” | Existing useful routes become unavailable during refresh. Keep the list usable, identify it as saved content, and place refresh status beside it. | [Loading — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/loading#Best-practices) supports useful content and background loading without interrupting interaction. A spinner is appropriate for unknown duration; obscuring useful content and leaving an unexplained wait are the problems. |
| 4 — Medium | “a fake 90% bar never advances” | The completion estimate is misleading. Remove fabricated percentages; show an animated indeterminate indicator until work ends. | [Progress indicators — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators#Best-practices) requires honest reporting across the whole operation and warns against an early rush to 90%. Determinate progress is preferred only when measurable. |
